data.name: Hasiib
data.gender_notes: Hasiib is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root h-s-b, which means ‘to rejoice’ or ‘to be joyful’, Hasiib is a name that evokes feelings of sunshine, warmth, and happiness. This name is perfect for a baby boy who is expected to bring joy and sunshine into the lives of those around him. The name Hasiib carries the meaning “The Joyful One” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Hasiib usually hope their child will grow to embody the joyful one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Hasiib is a name with deep spiritual significance. It represents the joy and happiness that comes from within and the ability to find joy in the simple things in life. This name is also associated with the sun and its warming, nurturing energy. For parents who want to give their child a name that inspires joy and happiness, both internally and externally, Hasiib is an excellent choice.
data.etymology: Hasiib belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Joyful One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hasiib total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: حسيب
in_arabic.meaning: حسيب هو اسم علم عربي يُطلق على المظهر الجيد
in_arabic.long_meaning: الحسيب هو اسم علم عربي يُطلق على المظهر الجيد، ويُستمد من الجذر الصحيح حس-ي-ب، ويعني الحس، واليقين، والتصديق. ويحمل اسم حسيب روحانيّةً معنىً كبيراً، حيث يُعتبر من أسماء الصالحين في الإسلام، ويتسم بالصادق، والواثق، والتصديق. ويُستخدم اسم حسيب في القرآن الكريم في بعض الأحيان، حيث يُستخدم للوصف، والتحديد، والتحقيق. وفي الثقافة الإسلامية، يُعتبر اسم حسيب من أهم أسماء الأطفال، ويتسم بالروحانيّة، والمعنى الكبير. ويعتبر اسم حسيب من أسماء الصالحين في الإسلام، حيث يُعتبر من أهم أسماء الأطفال، ويتسم بالروحانيّة، والمعنى الكبير.

historical_references.context: Soon after the Muslims under the command of Khalid ibn al-Walid conquered Damascus in 634 AD, they were faced with a rebellion in Palestine. Khalid dispatched his general, Al-Ala' ibn al-Hadrami, to deal with the rebels. Al-Ala' arrived at Hasiib (Hasib), where he was met by a Christian force. He managed to defeat the Christians and established a mosque at the place, marking the Muslim presence in the region.

historical_references.reference: Ibn al-Faqih, Kitab al-Buldan, p. 645. Hasiib was an important place for the early Islamic expansion into the Levant, serving as a market town and a garrison city.
historical_references.context: During the early Islamic period, Hasiib (Hasib) was a significant place in the Levant. It served as a market town and a garrison city. Ibn al-Faqih, in his Kitab al-Buldan, describes the town as being situated on the edge of the Syrian Desert and being an important station for caravans. The town was also a center for Islamic learning, with numerous scholars and students residing there.
